Definition: something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price:--money, riches.
BiblicalUsage: Money is called needful things in the New Testament, and Jesus warns how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter the kingdom. Barnabas lays the price of his field at the apostles' feet, and Simon offers money to buy the power of the Spirit. The same word covers honest provision and the attempt to purchase what cannot be bought.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe money is a tool that turns into a master the moment we trust it. Barnabas shows its right use, and Simon shows its wrong one, and the difference is worship. My position is that wealth is never the problem on its own — trusting it is.
